  (`submodule.c:L2080-L2091`), and the section's name where it has no `path` key (`:L1953`).
  libgit2 refuses that path only where a component is `.` or `..` (`:L479-L498`, `:L2204`;

  holds `.git` (`submodule.c:L691`, `:L2225-L2231`). So `submodule.<name>.path` is a path
  libgit2 takes from a config file during the status read, and it is the sixth member. The adapter's own comment says the same: "Only an include key follows a path to a file. A submodule section's own `path` is decided below" (`crates/ka-reader-core/src/git_reader/libgit2.rs:L260-L261`, at `ka-reader@1d5c3cf`). *(Until 2026-10-07 this sentence quoted a comment that read "only includes follow paths", at `libgit2.rs:L236-L237` at `ka-reader@5f3e895`, and said the source and the measurement below say otherwise; `git grep -n -i 'only includes follow' 1d5c3cf -- crates` prints nothing. `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-41.md` § 5.4; RN-106.)*
  *Its spelling and its refusals.* Before the status read the adapter spells the path of every

  observation, with the key and the path as the file spells them. A value beginning `/` is
  refused without being located. libgit2 drops the leading `/` and joins the value under the
  working tree (`libgit2/src/util/str.c:L778`, `:L830`; `repository.c:L3247`), and the

  lines), and the adapter spells it from the working tree. A section with no `path` key is decided on its name, and its refusal carries the section word as the file writes it — `submodule`, `Submodule` (`crates/ka-reader-core/src/git_reader/config_scan.rs:L59-L60`) — as the key and the name as the path, never `submodule.<name>.path` (`libgit2.rs:L302-L311`; `[submodule "../outside-n"]` answers `ConfigNamesOutside` with key `submodule` and path `../outside-n`, `crates/ka-reader-core/tests/git_state.rs:L2748`). Every value is spelled from the working tree of the level whose `.gitmodules` holds it — a section in an included file too (`:L2893`) — and a verified submodule's from its own working tree (`:L2939`). *(Until 2026-10-07 this sentence read "What the condition carries as the key for a section that has no `path` key is the design of the change that builds the check". `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-37.md` § 2.1; RN-102; `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-41.md` § 5.4; RN-106.)*
  **The status read and the submodule map.** The status read reports each gitlink from the
  repository at that gitlink's own path, and it opens no repository the adapter has not
  verified. libgit2 does not hold either half by itself. It keys the map by section name
  (`submodule.c:L2211`) and looks a gitlink up by its path in the same map
  (`diff_generate.c:L771`; `submodule.c:L346`). Where a section's name is a gitlink's path and

  *Measured.* The run that answered the item called the adapter built from the tree at
  `ka-reader@bd382c8`, against `libgit2-sys 0.18.8+1.9.7`, on four folders. Each is a repository
  with a gitlink `sub` in its index and a clean repository at `sub`
  (`docs/trail/sdd/self_answer-49.md`, *The measurement*, which holds the scenes and how to
  repeat them). With `[submodule "sub"] path = link/x`, `link` a link to a directory outside
  the folder and a repository at `x` there, `status()` listed `sub` as modified. With nothing
  at `x` it listed no `sub`. Those two scenes differ only in what lies outside the folder, so
  the status read opened a repository outside the folder. With `path = evil` and a second
  repository at `evil` inside the folder, `status()` listed `sub` as modified where
  `git status --porcelain` printed only `?? evil/`. The probe answered `root` and `status()`
  answered with its lists on all four. The fold that wrote this paragraph did not repeat the
  measurement. `git diff --quiet bd382c8 5f3e895 -- . ':!docs'` exits 0, so the two commits
  hold one tree outside `docs/`.
  *The response.* The adapter refuses the status read where a section of `.gitmodules` would
  make libgit2 open, or report, another location for a path that read looks up. Verifying the
  other repository and then running status was not taken. It restores containment and leaves
  the list reporting another repository's state under the gitlink's name. § 3's `git-reader`
  row already refuses a status run with a submodule left out, "because the list would then
  read as whole". Reading a list that names another repository's state as the same failure
  is reasoning.
  *The condition.* The refusal answers a condition of its own: `.gitmodules` gives a submodule
  path the status read looks up another location. It is not the config condition, because
  neither of that condition's observations is true of a path that spells inside the folder.
  It carries the section's name and its path as the file spells them, and the log line holds
  no path. It crosses SM-2, SM-4 and SM-8 as the config condition does. It meets `status()`
  alone: the probe answers `root`, `state()` answers, and the whole Git item is `failed` with
  this condition, as § 3 `GitState` states for a failure of either read (§ 6 S-4 *Reached

  adapter and the shell's sentences in-process; no case runs either on the built bundle. *(Until
  2026-10-07 this paragraph was headed "A known defect, until a change lands" and said that at
  `ka-reader@66f428d` the adapter answered one condition for both observations, the case for
  `relative/objects` asserted that condition, and the shipped sentence and the model's phrase
  said *outside* for it, which for an entry that leads into the opened folder was false.
  `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-40.md` § 5.1; RN-105.)* *(Until 2026-10-06 the paragraph stated one
  observation, for every refused entry. `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-38.md` § 5.3; RN-103.)*
  *Where the check runs, and what it reads.* It runs where the config check runs: on the
  probe, and before the open behind `state()` and `status()`. libgit2 opens the object store on
  first use and not during the open, by the answer's reading of `repository.c:L1535-L1573`,
  which this fold did not open. The check is placed with the config check all the same, so
  that one check runs in one place. It reads `objects/info/alternates` under the common
  directory. A link at `objects`, `info` or `alternates` whose spelling leaves the folder is
  refused without a read, so a linked `objects` directory that leads out is refused here. The
  check then reads the `info/alternates` file of each alternate that spells inside the folder,
  because libgit2 loads each added object directory's own alternates file (`odb.c:L758`,
  `:L800`). libgit2 stops at a depth of five (`odb.c:L27`, `:L770`). A chain deeper than five,
  a file over the size bound, or a link chain over the walk's bound is refused.
  *The spellings follow libgit2's own rule* (`odb.c:L789-L802`). An empty line and a line
  beginning `#` are skipped (`:L790-L791`). An entry beginning `.` is spelled from the objects
  directory that holds the file (`:L794-L798`). An absolute entry is taken as written. Any
  other entry libgit2 passes on as written (`:L800`), so the operating system resolves it
  against the process's working directory and not against the folder. Git reads the same entry
  from the object directory that holds the file: its documentation says relative paths are
  "relative to the object database, not to the repository!"
  (`https://git-scm.com/docs/gitrepository-layout`, `objects/info/alternates`, read through a
  fetch on 2026-10-06), and under git 2.54.0 an entry `store` was read from `.git/objects/store`
  with the shell's working directory elsewhere (`docs/trail/sdd/self_answer-50.md` § 5.3, *The
  measurement*). So the entry has two places it can lead, and the adapter locates neither and
  reads no working directory: `grep -rn 'current_dir\|getcwd\|set_current_dir' crates
  ka-reader-mac/Sources` prints three lines at `ka-reader@66f428d`, all under `tests/`. Such an entry
  is refused without being located (*The condition*, above). A leading space and a leading `~`
  put an entry in this form, because nothing is trimmed and nothing is expanded
  (`alternates_scan.rs:L24-L27`; `odb.c:L789-L800`). *Locating it was considered and not taken:*
  spelled from the working directory, the answer would depend on what launched the process;
  spelled from the object directory, it would follow Git and pass a place libgit2 does not read,
  so a pass would let libgit2 `stat` a place the adapter did not check. Any one refused entry
  refuses the repository. *(Until 2026-10-06 this passage said such an entry "is refused as
  outside". `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-38.md` § 5.3; RN-103.)*
  *What is not a refusal.* No alternates file passes (`odb.c:L776-L779`). A file holding only
  empty lines and comments passes. An entry that spells inside the folder with nothing there
  passes, because libgit2 skips an alternate it cannot `stat` (`odb.c:L697-L700`). That sentence
  does not reach an entry the adapter does not locate, which is refused whether or not anything
  is there (*The condition*; RN-103). An alternates
  file the adapter cannot read answers the existing condition for an unreadable Git directory.
  *What the refusal costs a reader.* A clone made with `git clone --shared`, or with
  `--reference` from a repository on the same machine, keeps an alternates file that names the
  source repository's objects (`https://git-scm.com/docs/git-clone`, the `--shared` and
  `--reference` options, read through a fetch on 2026-10-04). Where the source lies outside the
  opened folder, that clone shows a failed Git item with the cause, while `git status` in a
  terminal works. This follows from `docs/fdr.md` R-101 as it stands (`docs/fdr.md:L188`), as
  the two differences § 3's `git-reader` row names do: showing that clone's status means
  reading objects outside the folder. Leaving the read unrefused would not show the status
  either. In the bundle the sandbox denies the `stat`, libgit2 then skips the alternate with no
  error (`odb.c:L697-L700`), and a status read that needs an object held there has nothing that
  names the cause. That sequence is read from the source and was not run. A repository whose
  alternates file carries an entry beginning with neither `.` nor `/` shows a failed Git item
  where `git status` in a terminal works, because Git reads the entry from the object directory
  (*The spellings*; RN-103).
  *Submodules.* Each submodule repository has an object store of its own, so the verification
  before the status read gains this check beside its two (§ 3, the `git-reader` row). Whether
  the status read opens a submodule's object store was not read in the source. The check runs
  on each submodule whichever is the case, because it reads only inside the folder.
  *The proof.* One fixture whose alternates file names an objects directory outside the
  fixture, and one case showing that directory is not read. Both are in the tree at
  `ka-reader@66f428d`. The fixture is `checks/fixtures/alternates-names-outside`, with
  `alternates-names-outside.git.tar`, whose `.git/objects/info/alternates` holds the one line
  `../../../elsewhere/objects`. The case is
  `test_the_outside_object_directory_is_never_read_on_the_three_calls`
  (`crates/ka-reader-core/tests/git_state.rs:L1733`). It makes a FIFO at the outside object
  directory's `info/alternates` and asserts that none of the three calls opened it
  (`:L1715-L1726`, `:L1742-L1746`): that file is what a load of the object directory would open,
  and it is the watch the config cases make (*The proof, and what no case holds yet*, above). It
  watches that one file. It does not watch a `stat` of the directory, which is the first thing
  libgit2 does to an alternate (`odb.c:L697`); that no `stat` is made rests on the order in the
  code, where the check runs before the open (`libgit2.rs:L112-L115`), and not on the case. The
  case runs the adapter in-process, and no case runs the check on the built bundle. The fold that
  wrote this paragraph ran `cargo test --workspace --locked` on the tree at `ka-reader@5331b85`,
  whose tree outside `docs/` is `ka-reader@66f428d`'s, and it printed 499 passed and 0 failed. So in
  the harness the alternates read is a held property, and on the bundle the check has not been
  run. *(Until 2026-10-06 this paragraph said no fixture carried an alternates file, on a `grep`
  that printed nothing at `ka-reader@3b6754d`, and that the read was a stated limit until the case
  existed. `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-38.md` § 5.1; RN-103.)*
  *Not reached, and no change made.* The `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` environment
  variable also names object directories. The answer's reasoning reads libgit2 as consulting it
  only for a repository opened from the environment, and the adapter as never opening that way
  (`docs/trail/sdd/self_answer-47.md`, "The environment path"). This fold opened the adapter's
  open, which passes `NO_SEARCH` and no environment flag
  (`crates/ka-reader-core/src/git_reader/libgit2.rs:L81`, at `ka-reader@3b6754d`), and did not open
  the libgit2 lines.
  **Until the checks are built.** Both checks before the open are built. The config check is in
  the tree at `ka-reader@fc14574`, with the two cases *The proof* names. The alternates check is in
  the tree at `ka-reader@66f428d`: `check_alternates`
  (`crates/ka-reader-core/src/git_reader/libgit2.rs:L303`), called before `open_at` in the helper
  behind `state()` and `status()` (`:L114`), on each verified submodule (`:L449`) and on the
  probe (`:L475`), with the case *The proof* under "A third way out" names. Those cases run the
  adapter in-process, and no case runs either check on the built bundle. The same held for each
  read until its check landed: from the first build in which `mac-shell` calls `ka_reader_read_git`
  (`ka-reader@129586e`; § 4 C-I3) until the config check landed, the bundle opened a reader's own
  repositories with the sandbox as the only bound on the config-named read, and a repository
  whose config names an outside path showed a failed Git item if libgit2's open or status read
  did not survive the refusal (§ 6 S-4 *Reached when*, observable half, "Git state the tool could
  not read"); and until the tree at `ka-reader@66f428d` the sandbox was the only bound on the
  alternates read in the bundle, and nothing bounded it in the harness, so that read was a stated
  limit of § 4 C-D1 outside the sandbox and not a held property. From the tree at `ka-reader@772c63b` the adapter refuses the status read before the submodule map opens a repository outside the folder, or reports one from another location inside it, so in the harness those reads are held properties and the sandbox is no longer the only bound on any read this risk names (*The sixth member*, *Built, and the cases that hold it*, above; RN-106). *(Until 2026-10-07 this sentence read "The sandbox is now the only bound on one read: the repository the submodule map opens outside the folder". `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-41.md` § 5.1; RN-106.)* (RN-87; `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-26.md` § 5.4,
  RN-91; `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-27.md` § 5.1, RN-92; `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-34.md` §§ 5.1 – 5.4,
  RN-99; `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-35.md` § 2.1, RN-100; `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-36.md` § 5.2,
  RN-101; `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-38.md` § 5.1, RN-103). *(Until 2026-10-06 this paragraph said no build bounds the config-named read before
  its check lands, in the present tense. RN-101.)* *(Later on 2026-10-06 it said the alternates
  check was not built and that the sandbox was still the only bound on the alternates read.
  `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-38.md` § 5.1; RN-103.)* The `.gitmodules` check is a third check, and at `ka-reader@1d5c3cf` it is built whole: for the file's include keys from `ka-reader@5f3e895`, and for each section's path and for the submodule map from `ka-reader@772c63b`, the merge that landed them (*The sixth member*, *Built, and the cases that hold it*, above; RN-102, RN-106). *(Until 2026-10-07 this sentence said the check was built for the file's include keys and not for a section's path, and that the refusal on the submodule map was not built. `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-37.md` § 2.1; RN-102; `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-41.md` § 5.1; RN-106.)*

- **R-17:** The floor follows the hosted runner's lifetime — C-R5 grounds the value in the one macOS
  the `macos-26` image and the maintainer's Mac run, so the image's retirement is the floor's next
  move, set by a vendor's calendar and not by the stack or the product — *shows up as* a GitHub
  changelog entry retiring the `macos-26` image, with brownout windows before the date — the shape
  of https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-01-github-actions-macos-14-runner-image-retirement/,
  which gave 32 days from its 2026-10-01 post to the 2026-11-02 retirement and failed jobs in eight
  windows before it — or as a CI run that fails in a brownout window with no change under it;
  *response* the floor is the owner's to move, and the move is a companion item on this document in
  the owner's hand, as the 14.0 → 26.0 move was (`docs/trail/sdd/cycle-43.md` § 5.1); before 1.0.0
  the move is the plist line, the manifest's platform, the deployment target and the walk, and after
  1.0.0 it is a major under C-6, with `checks/contract.sh` red on the pin until one is cut (R-12);
  `docs/nfdr.md` QC-56 and `docs/fdr.md` R-133 are re-derived in their seats' rounds, the route this
  move's companions took (`ka-reader@55c04de:docs/architecture_open_issues.md` § 2.1,
  `ka-reader@2629164:docs/fdr_open_issues.md` § 2.1). What the design does not do: pin CI to an
  image below the floor to keep adopters, because then no hosted run runs the app on its floor — the
  gap the owner closed; or run on `macos-latest`, C-R5's alias rule.

## 12. What this design is not

<The boundaries, so a reader does not look here for something this document never held.

Above: it never changes product goals or scope (the PRD), system requirements (the SRS), or the
experience (the UXD). A gap in any of them is an open issue in the companion, not a rewrite here.

Below: it authors no ADR. The architecturally-significant decisions are **surfaced**; the Principal
Architect records them, and this SDD references those ADRs once they exist. It designs no individual
change — that is the delivery-tier Architect's `change_design.md`, one change at a time against the
system defined here.

**What "surfaced" means, exactly:** the Principal Architect reads three surfaces of this document and
no fourth — **§ 2's shape table** (each alternative's *right when / wrong when / taken?* row),
**§ 9's trade-offs**, and **the SDD Review Notes**. That is the set, not a sample: a run that has
written those three has surfaced everything the recorder will look for. What earns a record, how one
is written, and what to do with a decision visible in the design but argued in none of the three are
`<CORE>/prompts/principal_architect_create_architecture.md`'s, not this section's.>

**The PRD boundary** — the CPO's clause.

This design changes no product goal and no scope. Every PRD section cited above is cited as
`docs/PRD.md` v18 (Settled) states it *(v15 here until v68, though v16 reached this document at v51
— RN-112 — and v17 – v18 through `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-62.md` §§ 1.1 – 2.2; RC-8)*; the cut in § 6 delivers what the PRD names and nothing it
excludes, and § 1 holds every slice to the finish line the PRD is scoped against. The PRD delegates no
value to this document directly — its delegations run through the SRS (the acquisition channel,
the macOS floor) and this document takes the SRS's word for them. A gap in the PRD found here is a
companion item for the CPO's own PRD run, never a rewrite from this document — **even by the seat
that holds the PRD's pen in that run**. One gap was found and went to the companion, not into the
PRD: what the 1.0.0 promise covers for an application with no library surface, which
§ Assumptions "Versioning" names as "what users rely on" and does not define — answered
**confirm** by the owner, 2026-09-04, and folded (`docs/trail/sdd/cycle-2.md` § 2.2, RN-19); the
PRD is unchanged by the answer, and the contract lives in § 6 S-12. One further item is not a gap but a call the PRD leaves open by design — "Before 1.0.0
anything may change" — raised as the owner's cut call (`docs/trail/sdd/cycle-1.md` § 3.1) and
answered *keep* on the owner's own prior ruling (RN-17). One item touched the promise itself
without opening a gap: a network entitlement was found to make the shipped window draw
(`docs/trail/sdd/cycle-8.md` § 5.1), and the owner's answer held the PRD's line — "no network
call at all during operation" (`docs/PRD.md` § Data & Privacy) — as the operating system's
refusal and not the code's, so the PRD is unchanged and the mechanism moves in § 4 C-R2, never
here. The item that ruling left open — the renderer that cannot start under it — is answered:
the renderer leaves WKWebView (`docs/trail/sdd/cycle-9.md` § 1.1, the owner, 2026-09-23), and it
opens no PRD gap either: the PRD names no renderer, its § Dependencies / Integrations naming the

the beta (PRD v17 – v18 § Scope (In)) moved the first public release's place and the cut around

**The SRS boundary.** This design changes no requirement. Every `FR-n`, `NFR-n`, `DR-n` and `C-n`

## SDD Review Notes

<This section is the SDD's **creation trail** — every load-bearing element carries a written *why*.
An element derived from an upstream document carries its why inline, as its *Traces to* tag;
**everything the upstream documents did not settle carries its why here**, with its reason: an
invented value, an owner's answer folded from the open-issues file, a best-effort choice drafted by
one of the three seats, or a place where a contradiction between the SRS and the UXD was resolved
the SDD's own way.

On a revision **or a recreate**, **every change to already-settled content carries the legitimate
reason that authorized it** — an owner answer or directive, or an upstream change. Settled content
is all of it: the shape, the seams, the cut, and the existing wording of these notes. A change with
no findable legitimate reason is a bug and should not appear in the SDD at all.

A genuine product-intent gap is *not* recorded here — it goes to the open-issues companion for the
owner. Once the owner answers, capture the answer here, because the companion is deleted when the
round finishes clean and this trail is the durable provenance.

Each note names the seat that made the call and its relation to the upstream documents: *added* (the
SDD states something they do not) or *changed* (it departs from what they say).>

- **RN-52:** *(CTO)* *(changed)* The owner's cycle-8 ruling is folded on this seat's four lanes,
  and the mechanism it asked for (answer 3) is found and is not a configuration. **The
  mechanism.** WebKit's XPC services — Networking, GPU, and the content process that needs them —
  check the host's entitlements at their own start: `XPCServiceInitializerDelegate::checkEntitlements()`
  returns true at once when the host holds `com.apple.security.network.client`, and otherwise,
  for a sandboxed host, calls `sandbox_check_by_audit_token(…, "mach-lookup", …,
  "com.apple.nsurlsessiond")` on the host's audit token and, on a non-zero result, logs
  `RELEASE_LOG_FAULT(Network, "Application does not have permission to communicate with network
  resources. rc=%d : errno=%d", …)` and returns false
  (https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/bb75cbc0003033ea73c42ef02370767aa52d6ba6/Source/WebKit/Shared/EntryPointUtilities/Cocoa/XPCService/XPCServiceEntryPoint.mm,
  `checkEntitlements`, under `#if PLATFORM(MAC) || PLATFORM(MACCATALYST)`). WebKit's own comments
  on those lines: "Remove this check once WebKit can work without network access" and "This
  requirement is too strict, it should be possible to load file:// resources without network
  access" (`rdar://problem/54178641`). On this Mac, `/usr/bin/log show --start "2026-09-23
  01:31:20" --end "2026-09-23 01:32:50" --style compact --predicate '(process CONTAINS[c]
  "WebKit" OR …)'` — the owner's first sampling window — prints `com.apple.WebKit.GPU[87803] …
  (WebKit) Application does not have permission to communicate with network resources. rc=1 :
  errno=34` at 01:31:24.109, then the same line from `com.apple.WebKit.Networking` pids 87805,
  87810, 87813, 87816, … every 15–30 ms to the window's end, all under `ka-reader-app[87785]`
  launched at 01:31:23; the 02:12 window reads the same under `ka-reader-app[39010]` and
  `ka-reader-app[42457]`. So the content process's `processDidTerminateOrFailedToLaunch` in the
  owner's sample is the network process refusing to initialize and being relaunched: the
  requirement is WebKit's, on the host's entitlements, in the process-launch path — reachable by
  no `tauri.conf.json` key, no `wry` setting and no line of this product's, and the cycle-8
  table's last two rows are the two host states that pass the check. Corroborated, not derived:
  FB6993802, filed 2019-08-11 against macOS 10.14.6 and open
  (https://github.com/feedback-assistant/reports/issues/1); Apple's forum thread of the same year,
  where the only route named is the deprecated in-process WebView
  (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/116359); Tauri's docs issue reporting a white screen
  in sandboxed apps without the entitlement (https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri-docs/issues/3171).
  **What that leaves.** Answer 3's own clause — "if the fix needs no entitlement, the list
  stands" — does not decide this case, because the fix needs the one entitlement answer 1 refuses,
  or its mach-lookup twin, which this seat reads as refused with it (RC-2 names it so the owner's
  refusal is the owner's and not assumed). So C-R1 and ADR-0002 (the system WKWebView) and C-R2
  as the ruling writes it cannot both stand, and the choice is the owner's on two grounds: the
  runtime was confirmed by the owner (`ka-reader@70a879a:docs/trail/sdd/cycle-1.md` § 2.2), and
  ADR-0002 states the renderer technology is not replaceable inside the terminus
  (`docs/fdr.md` PD-29). It is the companion's § 1.1, with the exits priced and this seat's
  position — the renderer leaves WKWebView, because the wall is the product and the renderer
  wall was always the cheaper of the two to lose (§ 2, row 4) — held there, not in the lanes.
  **C-R2** is rewritten to the rule, with the v1 members kept under it — the same three members
  ADR-0003 names, so S-7's "two entries" and S-10's and S-11's "three entries" stay true and are
  not touched; *Violated by* is rescoped from "a slice that adds an entitlement" to a network
  entitlement of any kind, an entitlement with no record, and a probe report of either denial
  allowed, because the rule admits an entitlement with a record and the old clause forbade
  exactly that. **The gate** (answer 4) is C-I3's new clause and a new script,
  `checks/renderer.sh`, not a branch of `checks/bundle.sh`: that script has one job and refuses
  to launch anything but C-R2's set (`checks/bundle.sh`, its header), and the wall gate must keep
  its meaning when the renderer gate is red. Its observable is the host inside `open_folder` —
  the owner's floor, "at the least, that the page reached `open_folder`" — because it is the
  renderer's first and only unconditional call (`ka-reader@a4ab8e6:ka-reader-ui/src/main.ts:L14-L19`)
  and it parks in the panel (`ka-reader@a4ab8e6:crates/ka-reader-app/src/main.rs:L17-L19`), so a
  bounded window catches it the way
  C-I3's window catches the sandbox report. It is read from the operating system or the process
  and never from a line the product writes, for two reasons: C-I2's log holds failed and stopped
  items and nothing else, and a marker written for a check is the class of evidence RC-1 stopped
  reading. The mechanism named is the one already measured — a thread sample showing
  `pick_folder → run_on_main` (`docs/trail/sdd/cycle-8.md` § 5.1) — and the script fixes it, as
  C-I3 leaves the bound to `checks/bundle.sh`; the hosted runner is an *Open Questions* item on

  **What was wrong.** A libgit2 repository open adds the global, XDG, system and programdata
  config levels, and under the App Sandbox takes the global level's home from the password
  entry. Those files lie outside the granted folder and the container, and C-D1's *Violated by*
  names any read there. The one call that stops them, `git2::opts::set_search_path`, is an
  `unsafe fn`. `ka-reader-core` holds no `unsafe` and only `git-reader` could name the binding, so
  no unit could make the call.

  refused, and this fold refuses it too. **§ 5.2 — what the held expansion and selection hold when the

  the model holds — and not § 4 C-E2's, the CDO's column, which already binds the surface's half and
  does not move. *Because* the rule is already the model's — a `Delta` carries "the place and the Git
  item … as they were" (`folder_model.rs:L405-L407`) and `reduce` carries the place from its input and
  rebuilds nothing from the listings (`:L772`) — and because the first form fails what this slice is

  an agent's rewrite — and a node that comes back collapsed is the refresh taking the place away,
  § 4 C-E2's *Violated by*, `docs/fdr.md` R-78's sentence and `docs/SRS.md` FR-27's. Not the third,
  because a row for an entry its parent's listing no longer carries is state the bridge did not send
  from a read — the `surfaces` row allows one exception and this would be a second — and the "marked

  its sentence (`:L349-L350`), for the window before the parent re-lists, and R-80 gives the open file
  its own; a held ghost row after the parent re-lists would add a third sentence nothing upstream asks
  for. **Consequence one, measured, and the reason the answer is a clause and not a sentence.** The
  held *listing* under a removed folder is not the place and is not kept as current. At
  `ka-reader@8ef8c5b` `reduce` touches only listings whose folder a reported path's parent resolves
  to (`apply_delta`, `:L669-L705`), so a removed folder's own listing stays, and a folder expanded
  over `a.rs`, removed and reported removed, then recreated holding `b.rs` and reported present,
  answers `listing("src")` as `["a.rs"]` with `b.rs` on disk. Drawn under the returned,
  still-expanded folder, that is stale content presented as current — R-81, UX-I4 — which R-78 does
  not license. So the row states the reducer's rule — an entry reported removed drops every held
  listing at and under its path, the listings and never the place; an entry reported present at a
  path the place holds expanded is read in that same delta, so the folder returns fresh or `pending`,
  never old — and names the tree at `8ef8c5b` a known defect against it until a change lands, with
  `follow-the-folder`'s command half holding the case. Both are SM-5's and move no seam.
  **Consequence two, a bound.** `admit` refuses a path that does not resolve (`:L710-L714`), so
  `expand` (`:L716`) and `collapse` (`:L732`) of an absent path leave the flag as it is, and no row is

- **RN-131:** *(CTO)* *(changed — S-7's history check, three bounds)* Item 2.2 of
  `docs/trail/sdd/cycle-63.md`, raised by a `companion-self-answer` run on 2026-11-06 and left to
  the CTO's seat (RN-129), was answered in that seat the same day (`ka-reader@0375085`; reasoning
  `docs/trail/sdd/self_answer-75.md` § 2.2): confirm, with three additions, all on S-7's command
  half. (1) The scan and the person's read cover every ref the public remote will hold, not the
  commits `main`'s HEAD reaches alone — a repository made public publishes every ref on the remote,
  and `git ls-remote --heads --tags origin` listed ten branches beside `main` and no tag on the day
  of the answer (re-read in this fold on the local remote-tracking refs, `git branch -r`: the same
  ten) — or the refs not to be published are deleted first and the release page says which. (2) The
  release page names the commit the read reached, and the public repository's `HEAD` at publication
  is that commit, so a commit landing after the read reopens the condition. (3) A finding is taken
  out of the history before publication, the read is repeated on the rewritten history, and the
  root-commit comparison is made against the checkout that repeated read passed on — a scrubbed
  history is still the project's own, which the PRD requires; a fresh copy is not. This seat adds
  one bound of its own, from § 3: the gate's *Secret scan* step scans the history HEAD reaches
  (the `read-only-harness` row), so the release condition is wider than the step, and whether the

## Open Questions

<A technical question this SDD leaves standing — recorded so a reader does not mistake silence for
an answer.

**This section is not the companion, and never a copy of it.** Anything awaiting the owner lives in
`SDD_open_issues.md` alone, and that file's **absence is the done signal**. An item written in both
has two homes and only one of them says when it is finished.

What belongs here is a question this SDD cannot close and is **not** asking the owner to close: one
that resolves downstream — in a slice, in a spike, or against a system that does not exist yet.

Omit this section entirely when there is nothing in it. An empty heading reads as an unanswered
question.>

- [OPEN: Whether a folder dropped on the Dock icon, or opened with *Open With*, is granted by the
  sandbox the same way as one chosen in the Open panel. Settled in the first slice by trying both
  against the built bundle; if not, C-R3 gains a clause saying those routes present the panel.]
- [OPEN: Whether libgit2 opens a repository correctly under a read-only user-selected grant with
  discovery disabled, for a plain `.git` folder and for a `.git` file naming a gitdir inside the
  grant. Settled by the first Git slice's `root_finding` and `git_state` fixtures running green
  on the built bundle; a failure is R-1 firing early. The same run shows the open answering
  `root` with the four machine-level config reads switched off (§ 3, the `core-bridge` row).
  Before the switch, a `stat` of a config path refused with anything but `ENOENT` or `ENOTDIR`
  is an error (`libgit2-sys 0.18.8+1.9.7`, `libgit2/src/libgit2/config.c:L143-L147`) and a
  failed config snapshot fails the open (`repository.c:L997-L999`); whether the sandbox's
  refusal took that path was never run. *(Extended on 2026-10-03; RN-87.)*]
